title: Origin of Shackles
next_chapter_hook: The name Chen Ji was clearly inscribed in the prophecy from ten thousand years ago, meaning his destiny was written from the very beginning—and the identity of that writer would overturn all his understanding.

text.content: The deepest part of the Tianji Pavilion ruins was a forgotten void. Chen Ji stepped through the final restriction, and his vision opened up—a massive circular stone chamber, its dome inscribed with star patterns as if sealing the entire night sky within. The air was thick with ancient dust, each breath feeling as heavy as devouring the weight of years. He looked around, his heartbeat involuntarily accelerating. The very existence of this space was a paradox—outside was clearly ruins and broken walls, yet here it remained perfectly intact, as if just sealed away.

dialogue.content: Young Master, the construction of this stone chamber...is identical to the internal runes of the Tianji Record. Master Mo's remnant soul trembled, rarely showing agitation: Your father searched for this place for decades, yet only returned with the first fragmentary page of the Tianji Record. And you... have actually made it here.

text.content: Chen Ji did not answer, his gaze fixed on the massive stone wall at the center of the chamber. The wall stood approximately thirty feet high and ten feet wide, entirely black as ink, yet flowing with fine silver patterns—ancient script, a prophetic language that had been lost tens of thousands of years before his birth. Each stroke seemed alive, subtly writhing, emitting an ancient aura that struck terror into the heart. The Tianji Record fragment in his embrace began to vibrate intensely.

dialogue.content: These characters... Master Mo, can you read them? Chen Ji's voice was calm, but the knuckles of his fingers gripping the fragment had turned white. Intuition told him the answer might be heavier than he could imagine.

Barely... This is the prophetic script of the Heavenly Dao Era, each character containing fragments of laws. Master Mo's voice turned hoarse: Young Master, please prepare yourself. What you are about to see is the shared fate of all prophetic seers throughout history—and this fate... seems to also concern you.

text.content: Chen Ji walked slowly toward the stone wall, and the silver patterns blazed brightly as he approached. The first chapter appeared before his eyes—records from nine thousand years ago, describing the brief yet glorious life of a prophetic seer called 'Mysterious机子'. He used the Tianji Record to peer into heavenly secrets, assisted three major sects through a catastrophe, yet died suddenly on the day of his triumph, the cause unknown. The second chapter recorded 'Xuanji Fairy' from six thousand years ago, equally falling at the peak.

dialogue.content: Young Master, do you see it? These people... were all the wielders of the Tianji Record throughout history. Without exception, they all died when the 'Key' awakened. Master Mo's voice turned sharp: The so-called 'Key' is the medium to open a certain forbidden door. And the prophetic seer's destiny is to become that key—after completing the mission, harvested by the Heavenly Will.

text.content: Chen Ji's expression remained unchanged, but a cold light flickered in the depths of his pupils. He continued reading downward. The third chapter, fourth chapter, fifth chapter... names flashed by one after another, each a once-dominant prophetic seer, each dying mysteriously after reaching their peak. Their methods of death varied, but the causes were strikingly similar—heavenly fate value dropping to zero, souls emptied by some force. And at the end of every record was the same phrase: 'The key is forged, returned to the Heavenly Dao.'

dialogue.content: So the price of the Tianji Record was never something as simple as consuming heavenly fate value from the beginning. Chen Ji chuckled lightly, his voice cold as a deep winter chill pool: The so-called prophetic ability is nothing but raising silkworms. Raising us into perfect keys, then harvesting us once and for all.

Young Master... Master Mo wanted to speak but stopped, his remnant soul flickering uncertainly in the air. After a long while, he spoke with difficulty: Your understanding is not wrong. But the resonance of the Tianji Record fragment indicates your connection to this place runs deeper than any previous wielder. He paused: Perhaps... there are other records.

text.content: Chen Ji pressed the Tianji Record fragment against the stone wall, and the silver patterns erupted with blinding light. Deep within the stone wall, a section of deliberately sealed text slowly emerged—the only golden text on the entire wall, the strokes like flowing liquid gold, emitting an aura entirely different from the laws of the Heavenly Dao. Master Mo's voice suddenly turned sharp: Impossible! These are Creation Inscriptions, content that can only be unlocked by the complete Tianji Record!

The golden text slowly reorganized before Chen Ji's eyes, transforming into meanings he could understand. 'I am the first wielder, using my life as the price, to inscribe the truth of the Heavenly Dao here. The Tianji Record was not created by the Heavenly Dao, but forged by ancient sages as a key embryo to oppose the Heavenly Will. All wielders throughout history are mere pieces, their fates already destined. Only those who break the destiny may—' The text ended abruptly, as if deliberately erased.

choice.prompt: Chen Ji stood before the erased prophecy on the stone wall, deep in thought. The fragment's glow continued, and a deeper connection was being established. He must make a choice—whether to forcibly trace the erased truth, or preserve his strength for future plans.

choices.description: Using one's heavenly fate value as the cost to forcibly trace the erased prophetic truth. May consume 10-15 points of heavenly fate.
choices.risk_hint: Heavenly fate is already scarce; consumption may affect subsequent arrangements

text.content: Chen Ji did not hesitate for an instant, pressing the fragment tightly against the stone wall. 'Trace.' The moment the words fell, heavenly fate value gushed out like a waterfall. Agonizing pain surged from the depths of his soul, as if countless needles simultaneously piercing his mental sea. But he gritted his teeth, allowing blood to seep from the corners of his eyes, forcibly dragging那段被抹去的文字 from the void.

dialogue.content: 'Only those who break the destiny may—' Chen Ji softly read out the remaining text, his pupils suddenly contracting. Because at the final position, a name appeared. A name that should not have appeared in a ten-thousand-year-old prophecy. Chen Ji.

choices.description: Stay calm, note the existing clues, and trace only after heavenly fate value is restored. Maintain the status quo and preserve strength.
choices.visible_reward: Retain heavenly fate value, maintain ability for subsequent arrangements
choices.risk_hint: May miss key information, allowing opponents to strike first

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing himself to look away. Heavenly fate value was nearly depleted, and this environment was full of unknowns. He would not act recklessly with incomplete information—that was something only fools would do. He stepped back three paces from the stone wall, returning the fragment to his embrace, and began to sort through the known information.

dialogue.content: 'In the prophecy from ten thousand years ago, someone could break their destiny, and my name appears in it.' A cold light flashed in Chen Ji's eyes: Either my destiny was designed from the beginning, or... someone wants me to think so. Either way, it's a trap. A cold smile curved his lips: Interesting.

text.content: At this moment, a low rumble echoed from the depths of the stone chamber. The star patterns on the dome slowly rotated, and silver pillars of light descended from the heavens, converging before the stone wall into a blurry humanoid form. The figure had no face, only a pair of eyes composed of pure starlight, quietly gazing at Chen Ji. A vast and profound aura instantly enveloped the entire chamber—that was a pressure surpassing all cultivators—the projection of the Heavenly Will.

dialogue.content: 'Finally arrived.' The voice carried no emotional fluctuation, yet resounded directly in Chen Ji's mental sea: 'I've been waiting for you for a long time, Chen Ji.' The humanoid form in the light pillar took a step forward, the starlight eyes reflecting a kind of ancient and cruel scrutiny: 'The seed from ten thousand years ago, finally sprouted.'

Chen Ji stared directly at those starlight eyes, the corner of his lip反而勾起一抹淡笑. 'Eyes of the Heavenly Dao?' His voice was terrifyingly calm: 'So you can also be afraid. Afraid that someone might truly break your chess game, so you couldn't wait to come out and test.' He slowly raised his hand, the fragment flickering in his palm: 'This is a projection, not the main body, right?'

A barely perceptible fluctuation flickered in those starlight eyes. 'Clever.' The voice remained devoid of temperature: 'But clever people often die the fastest. You think you're making moves, not knowing every step you take is under my observation.' The light pillar slightly expanded: 'The Tianji Record chose you because you're special enough. But special... does not mean you'll survive until the end.'

text.content: Chen Ji did not retreat, instead taking a step forward. 'Then let's try.' His voice was cold as cold iron: 'Ten thousand years ago you couldn't stop the first prophetic seer from breaking destiny, and ten thousand years later you still can't stop me. All you can do is repeat the same tactics—raise the pieces until they're ripe, then harvest.' The fragment erupted with a blinding golden light, shooting directly toward the center of the light pillar.

choice.prompt: The moment the golden light struck the projection of the Heavenly Eyes, Chen Ji felt an unprecedented confrontation of power. This was the first clash directly confronting the Heavenly Will—he must decide his next strategy.

choices.description: While the projection is unstable, fully mobilize the Tianji Record to attack, probing the true strength of the Heavenly Eyes.
choices.visible_cost: May consume large amounts of heavenly fate value
choices.visible_reward: May force out more information from the Heavenly Eyes
choices.risk_hint: The gap in strength is vast, may suffer backlash

text.content: Chen Ji raised the fragment high above his head, pouring all his spiritual power into it. Golden light transformed into a sword blade, thrusting directly toward those starlight eyes. Wherever the blade passed, space crumbled inch by inch, revealing the black void behind it. However, the light pillar merely swayed gently.

dialogue.content: 'Ridiculous.' For the first time, emotion appeared in the voice of the Heavenly Eyes—naked mockery. 'You want to harm even a fragment of my projection?' The light pillar suddenly expanded, a devastating force pouring out, crushing Chen Ji's sword blade completely. He grunted, his form stumbling backward, blood seeping from the corner of his mouth.

choices.description: After assessing the strength gap between enemy and self, actively retreat, preserve heavenly fate value for future plans. As long as the mountains remain, there will be firewood.
choices.visible_reward: Preserve strength, maintain possibility for subsequent arrangements
choices.risk_hint: May be seen as cowardice, losing certain opportunities

text.content: Chen Ji's form flickered, retreating three steps backward. He did not continue attacking. Not that he couldn't, but that he disdain to. Though the Heavenly Eyes' projection was powerful, it was far from requiring him to risk his life. Moreover, his goal had never been to determine victory or defeat with a projection here. 'Today, let's consider it a greeting.'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji wiped the blood from the corner of his mouth, his smile反而更深了. 'Heavenly Eyes, you project yourself here, proving that my existence has made you uneasy.' He turned toward the stone chamber exit: 'Next time we meet, I hope it's the main body personally.' The light in those starlight eyes suddenly blazed, but before it could act, Chen Ji had already vanished into the shadows of the stone chamber.

text.content: Outside the chamber, the night was as dark as ink. Chen Ji stood atop the ruins of the Tianji Pavilion, letting the cold wind buffet his robes. The fragment in his chest had returned to calm, but he knew the real storm was only beginning. He lowered his gaze to his palm, where golden dust from the earlier clash still lingered. Each grain of dust was like a tiny star, slowly rotating in his palm. 'Heavenly Eyes...' he murmured to himself: 'So you can also be afraid.'

He slowly spread his palm, letting the golden dust flow between his fingers. Under the moonlight, his silhouette appeared lonely yet resolute. Tonight's discovery confirmed one thing—the Heavenly Eyes were not invincible existences; they could also feel fear and anxiety. And the root of this fear might be hidden within the final prophecy on that stone wall. Chen Ji raised his head toward the distant horizon, where lightning flickered vaguely within the clouds. His eyes reflected a cold, fierce light.
